we introduce a geometric yarn representation that is able to capture the yarn paths of a woven cloth and that is able to model the cloth appearance.
we present an approach to reverse engineer a cloth sample from a single image, estimate its geometric yarn model, and use this model as basis for a parametrized visual prototyping tool.
we introduce a novel geometric yarn model and a pipeline to reverse-engineer cloth from images.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to best represent cloth models, how to capture cloth samples, and how to edit cloth properties.
the automatic analysis of images of woven cloth, and the generation of realistic cloth models.
the development of an image based reverse engineering pipeline for woven cloth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our work is a step towards a more intuitive way to create realistic cloth simulations in computer graphics.
we have developed a novel approach to model cloth from a single image and we have shown that the model can be edited to produce realistic images of cloth with a wide variety of properties.
our method provides an intuitive, interactive and efficient approach to create parametric cloth models.

our approach allows the creation of a realistic visual prototype of cloth, that can be used for computer aided design of new cloth types.
we are able not only to capture the appearance of a given cloth sample, but also to edit it and generate new cloth samples.
we present a novel approach to reverse engineer cloth, and estimate a parametric model from a single input image.

we can create a parametrized model of a cloth sample from a single image that is physically plausible, realistic to look at and easy to edit.
